datasheet.title: Nokia ONT XS-010XR-P XGS-PON reverse powered ONT data sheet, CID212870

description: Temperature-hardened, reverse-powered XGS-PON single-family-unit ONT in a 208 x 142 x 34.3 mm white moulded housing, for a desk, a wall, or outdoors inside the Nokia outdoor ONT enclosure. The back edge carries a ground point, one 100M/1G/2.5G/5G/10GBASE-T RJ-45 that is also the PoE powered-device input, a pinhole reset, a round on/off button, the 12 V DC jack and the SC/APC PON port in a green adapter with a fibre-lock boss beside it. Three lamps on the top face read POWER, PON and DATA.

gaps.note: Product Guide Table 4-9 prints maximum power (not to exceed) 10.6 W. The data sheet CID212870 prints power consumption below 10 W. The manifest carries the guide's figure, the larger and the one that states its condition.
gaps.wanted: a Nokia statement of which figure is current

gaps.note: Figure 4-1 draws a round coaxial jack with a centre pin and the US kit's adapter is the XS-010X-R's 1AF32126AAAA; Table 4-6 says the power connection is a cable with a Molex connector, and Table 4-3 sells a Molex to Phoenix adapter with the outdoor enclosure. The manifest draws the figure.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of the POWER socket of a real unit

gaps.note: The guide's section 4.4 names a PoE 802.3af PD function; its section 4.3, the data sheet and the Quick Reference Guide say PoE+, and the data sheet writes PoE+ compliant powering (802.3af) in one line. The stated 10.6 W maximum is inside the 802.3af budget.
gaps.wanted: the PD class the port negotiates

gaps.note: The data sheet lists RJ-45 LEDs Mode/Status and Link/Carrier. No table gives their colours, which window is which, or their states; the Product Guide LED table covers only the three top-face lamps.
gaps.wanted: an LED table for the two jack lamps

gaps.note: The guide names an ONT SoC (Figure 4-4) without a part or a clock. Memory and flash are stated.
gaps.wanted: the SoC named in a Nokia document

gaps.note: No held picture shows the short side at the other end, so whether it is vented is not known.
gaps.wanted: a photograph or drawing of that side

gaps.note: no figure or render held shows the long edge opposite the ports
gaps.wanted: a photograph or drawing of the front edge

gaps.note: Figure 5-8 draws the first wall hole as an L of two slots, 17.5 x 7.0 and 7.0 x 11.5 mm, and the second as one slot 8.5 x 12.0 mm, each with a round screw position 9.0 mm across and a 9.0 mm ring. The device draws them as two shared keyhole parts, 6 x 10 mm each, with the round head 5.5 mm above the screw position, and the keyholes also sit upside down against the figure. Redrawing them as shown is a later part of its own and a one-way change, because leaving the shared part removes two placement ids.
gaps.wanted: a part that cuts the two holes, their rings and their screw positions as the figure shows them

gaps.note: Figure 5-8 shows a tab 8.9 mm wide at x 70.7 to 79.6 on the back edge, standing about 5.7 mm outside the 208 x 142 outline. Figure 4-1 draws a stub 16.5 mm wide at x 40.4 to 56.9. The library holds neither reading as measured. The kit has no shape for a feature outside a face's own rectangle: `chassis.overhang` and `chassis.ears` are for a rack device only, decor is clipped to the view's size, and `out` and `lift` give only a depth.
gaps.wanted: a drawing of the back edge that gives the tab's width

gaps.note: Figure 5-8 draws the case screw as a slotted head with one slot in a double ring. The device seats the shared screw head, which draws a cross. No slotted version exists in the library, and a new version of a shared part moves every device that seats it.
gaps.wanted: a slotted version of the shared screw head

controls.description: the on/off button and the reset pinhole; this box has no management port, so the group is what you press

leds.description: the three lamps on the top face

pon.description: the XGS-PON uplink, an SC/APC receptacle in a green adapter

rj45-10g.description: the one subscriber port, 100M/1G/2.5G/5G/10GBASE-T, and the PoE powered-device input

name: xs-010xr-p

bottom-layout.note: Product Guide Figure 5-8 p53, a plan of the underside, read at 600 dpi. GATE 1: outline 2140 x 1464 px, 10.29 and 10.31 px/mm against 208 and 142, orthographic to 0.2 percent. Four feet 11.65 mm across; two label recesses 60.4 x 40.7 and 60.4 x 20.8 mm, each with its lower right corner cut 2.2 mm; a plate 167.1 x 101.3 mm with corners of 7.8 mm radius; four slanted slots at 45 degrees, 15.0 x 5.5 mm, each in a dished recess; three wall-mounting holes with two screw positions (the first an L of two slots, 17.5 x 7.0 and 7.0 x 11.5 mm; the second one slot 8.5 x 12.0 mm; the third a slot 9.5 x 5.3 mm ending in a round 8.8 mm head; the first two stay the shared keyhole part, see the wall-hole-shapes gap, and the third is cut here); two round pegs 8.7 mm across, 9.0 mm from the front edge (Figure 5-12 p56 labels them rubber pads, fitted for the outdoor enclosure; no height is stated); thin creases from the plate corners to the housing corners. The file draws eight creases, nine paths: the one at the case screw is broken round the screw, as the figure draws it. The figure's double housing line is drawn as two, at 1.4 and 2.1 mm in. Each foot has the inner ring the figure draws, 10.0 mm across. A U ring recess surrounds the third wall hole, 12.3 mm across and open towards its round head. Each peg has the crescent of side wall below it in the figure, 2.5 mm deep, which the half turn puts on the plate side. These small shapes were read in the 600 dpi page at 4 times, rounded to 0.5 mm, and are estimates. Sizes are good to about 0.5 mm. The figure has the back edge at the bottom; this view has it at the top, so a figure point (x, y) is the face point (208 - x, 142 - y). Not drawn: the 8.9 x 5.7 mm tab the figure shows on the back edge at x 70.7 to 79.6, which stands outside the face's own 208 x 142 rectangle. Figure 4-1 draws a stub 16.5 mm wide at x 40.4 to 56.9 under the rear body.

chassis.note: Product Guide Table 4-8 p39, without the fibre storage tray: length 208 mm, width 142 mm, height 34.3 mm, 0.53 kg within 0.23 kg; with the tray 208 x 232 x 48 mm and 0.85 kg. The data sheet and the Quick Reference Guide print the same 208 x 142 x 34.3 and 0.53 kg. The ports are on a 208 mm edge (Figure 4-1 measures 2963 px across, and its RJ-45 then comes out 16.0 mm wide), so 208 is the width here and 142 the depth. Mount `desktop`: the guide stands it on a desk or shelf, hangs it horizontally on a wall by the keyholes in its underside or vertically on bracket 3FE49972AA, and outdoors seats it in outdoor enclosure 3FE54221AH; the feet-down way is the one drawn. THE HOUSING IS NOT A PLAIN BOX: its plan corners are rounded at about 19 mm (Figure 4-2) and its lower shell curves under below two seam lines; the views are the 208 x 142 x 34.3 envelope and the rounded outline is drawn on the top and bottom faces as a line.

colours.note: From the data sheet render, 975 x 481 px, by counting pixels: the housing reads #f7f7f7 on the back edge (3,600 px, median); 2,231 px of the PON adapter are green, median #68a80d; the legends are dark, #2f2f2f to #333333 at their darkest; the fibre-lock boss beside the PON port is brass-yellow, median #d1b830 over 232 px. A render, not a photograph of a unit.

dc-in-rating.note: Product Guide Table 4-2: 12 V DC 1 A at the DC jack - the `input-voltage` and `current-max-a` of the dc-in jack. The guide's block diagram calls it a 12 V barrel and states no barrel size; the jack is the library's one nominal `dc-barrel`.

lamps.note: Product Guide Table 4-7 p38. POWER green, blinking while firmware loads. PON green when up, green blinking while ranging, red when down (O7 or rogue), red blinking when out of range. DATA green at 100M/1G, yellow at 2.5G or above. The data sheet also lists two RJ-45 lamps, Mode/Status and Link/Carrier, with no colours or states. The lamp colours drawn are conventional hues for those words, not sampled.

power.note: Product Guide Table 4-9 p39: maximum power (not to exceed) 10.6 W, minimum 4.54 W, one 10GBASE-T Ethernet, other interfaces not provisioned. The Quick Reference Guide prints standby 4.6 W and typical 7.75 W; the data sheet prints below 10 W, recorded as a gap. Two feeds: the 12 V DC jack (12 V DC 1 A, Table 4-2) or PoE on the 10GE jack, which the guide calls a PoE 802.3af PD function and also POE+; the optional injector 1AF32488DA is 56 V 0.62 A.

power-jack.note: Drawn as the coaxial DC jack Figure 4-1 shows - a round socket with a centre pin - and the US kit ships the same adapter, 1AF32126AAAA, as the XS-010X-R, whose jack is drawn the same way. Table 4-6 calls the power connection a cable with a Molex connector; recorded as a gap.

rear-layout.note: Product Guide Figure 4-1 p36, an elevation of the back edge. x at 14.245 px/mm from the 208 width. GATE 1 IS ONLY HALF PASSED: the figure draws the top edge as a shallow arc and the shell 514 px from crest to underside, 36.1 mm at that scale against the stated 34.3, so heights are five percent out and are taken as fractions of 34.3; x is good to about 0.5 mm, y to about 1 mm. Centres left to right as seen from behind: ground point 21.3, 10GE 97.2, RESET 115.9, ON/OFF 132.6, POWER 148.3, PON 169.7, fibre-lock boss 180.3, laser mark 187.2. The RJ-45 is drawn 16.0 x 12.3 with its latch down and one lamp window in its lower left corner; the SC opening has its key slot up. Standard parts keep their registry sizes. The earth symbol is drawn 8.7 mm above the ground point; the library part that pairs the two holds them 6.5 mm apart, so the symbol sits about 2 mm low here.

side-layout.note: The guide speaks of side vents (5.5 step 1: 50 mm clearance from the side vents). Product Guide Figure 5-9 p53 shows a field of 22 slanted slats on the short side at the fibre end, which seen from the front is the left; the data sheet render shows only a faint vent texture at that end, too small to count. The figure draws two seams across the wall at the ends of the field; the two end seams are drawn at 19.0 and 122.8 mm. The figure draws no seam along the depth of this wall, so none is drawn on the left face. The right face keeps the two carried from the rear elevation (26.3 and 28.3 mm down). The slats are drawn on the left face as 2.3 x 21.0 mm stadiums at a 4.75 mm pitch, centred across the 142 mm depth and from 7.5 mm down the face. Scale: the field is taken to span the flat of the side between the 19 mm plan corners, 142 - 2 x 19 = 104 mm. The 22 slats then sit 4.75 mm apart, and the wall's 34.3 mm height, 238 px between its outer lines, sets the 6.9 px/mm that gives their length and start. The figure is a perspective view, so the figures are good to about 30 percent. No held picture shows the right side, so the right face carries no vents.

sources.note: Nokia ONT XS-010XR-P Product Guide, 3TN-00113-AAAA-TCZZA Issue 4 (BBD Release 25.01): Table 4-1 p33 the kits, Table 4-3 p34 the accessories, Table 4-8 p39 size and weight, Table 4-9 p39 power, Table 4-10 p39 the environment, Figure 4-1 p36 the back elevation, Figure 4-2 p38 the top plan, Figure 5-8 p53 the underside, Table 4-7 p38 the lamps. Nokia ONT XS-010XR-P data sheet CID212870 (the vendor datasheet) and Quick Reference Guide 3TN-00113-AAAA-TCZZB CID213181 for summary figures and the one product render. The guide figures are vector line art, read at 600 dpi.

top-layout.note: Product Guide Figure 4-2 p38, a plan of the front part of the top face at 15.13 px/mm from the 208 width; only the front edge is in the figure, so there is no second axis to check it against. Three lamps 1.8 mm across, 12.8 mm in from the front edge at 86.0, 103.9 and 121.9 mm - a row centred on the face at 17.95 mm pitch, drawn at 86, 104 and 122. Each legend runs away from its lamp towards the back, reading from the right. The data sheet render shows the same three and Figure 5-13 the same order.

wordmark.note: The data sheet render shows the vendor wordmark on the top face along the short edge at the right as seen from the front, reading along that edge. No line drawing shows it, so the reserved zone is placed by eye from a three-quarter render. Not drawn - a reserved logo zone: the wordmark is a mark, and marks are left to a later part of their own.
